what_it_does: Vector similarity search is the operation of finding, from a large collection of stored numerical vectors (lists of numbers that encode meaning — for example, how an AI represents a word or an image), the ones closest to a query vector. It is the core of recommendation engines and retrieval systems used alongside large language models. The bottleneck is memory bandwidth: to compare a query against millions of stored vectors, the system must read enormous amounts of data from DRAM (dynamic random-access memory, the main working memory of a computer) and ship it to the CPU, saturating the data bus. UPVSS offloads this work to UPMEM, a commercially available near-memory processing unit — a chip where small processors sit physically inside, or directly alongside, the DRAM modules so that arithmetic happens where the data already lives, eliminating most of the data movement. The paper designs an architecture-aware strategy for distributing the search workload across the many parallel UPMEM processors to exploit their aggregate memory bandwidth.
